title: An Internet for the KV Cache: Rethinking Classical Infrastructure Boundaries in the LLM Inference Age
event_hint: Vision for internet-scale, content-distribution management of LLM KV caches
problem: Agent, retrieval, tool-use, code, and multimodal workloads repeatedly revisit overlapping context, but model-side KV compression and system-side compute/storage/transfer optimizations evolve inside rigid cloud and datacenter boundaries. The resulting store-versus-recompute decision is not jointly optimized for model, network, application reuse, latency, and cost.
mechanism: The paper proposes decoupling compute and KV-cache storage across clouds and datacenters and treating the network as an active distribution channel. Compute/cache placement and store, transfer, recompute, or reuse decisions are driven by model metrics (prefill FLOPs, KV size), infrastructure metrics (GPU/storage/network costs and bandwidth), and application metrics (reuse frequency, tool-call duration, turns). It formalizes CacheCost versus PrefillCost and derives a break-even ratio for adaptive decisions.

evidence.claim: For a 1 GB KV cache over a fully utilized 10-Gbps Internet link, transfer takes about 0.8 seconds and costs roughly $0.09, versus about 15 seconds and $0.47 to recompute on an AWS 8×B200 GPU cluster.
In the example, transferring the cache is approximately 19x faster and 5.2x cheaper than recomputing it.
Compressed Sparse Attention is cited as reducing a 100,000-token DeepSeek cache from about 9 GB to 1 GB across one model generation.

The paper defines CacheCost as storage plus transfer cost for reusable KV and PrefillCost as the cost of recomputing prompt prefill, with a break-even ratio controlled by device cost, reuse frequency, transfer cost, GPU cost, peak FLOPS, prefill FLOPs, and cache size.

The authors argue the KV cache should be treated as a storage, communication, and scheduling primitive and that multiple store/recompute choices can be correct depending on infrastructure, application reuse, and model architecture.
evidence.baseline: KV cache as a local tensor optimization
evidence.source_locator: PDF pages 2-3, Our Vision and Section 3

evaluation_context: This is a systems-vision paper with an illustrative cost/latency example and analytical formulation rather than a deployed prototype. The example uses a 1 GB cache, 10-Gbps Internet link, AWS egress pricing, an AWS 8×B200 cluster, and DeepSeek-V4-Pro cache format; cited numbers are scenario estimates.
limitations: The 19x/5.2x comparison is a single illustrative scenario and assumes a fully utilized 10-Gbps link, particular AWS pricing, and recomputation on 8×B200 GPUs; network contention, cache hit probability, storage durability, and cross-provider policy are not measured. The proposal does not provide a prototype, scheduler implementation, end-to-end P95, or production deployment evidence. Break-even decisions are highly sensitive to reuse frequency, cache size, bandwidth, and GPU prices; partial reuse/recompute adds further complexity (inference).
project_relevance: This directly frames TPN as a joint cache placement and content-distribution problem: network bandwidth, latency, and price should be inputs to store/recompute decisions rather than post-hoc transport details. It suggests instrumenting KV reuse frequency, cache size, transfer price, prefill FLOPs, and application turn/tool duration alongside TTFT/TPOT, and evaluating break-even policy under changing network tiers (inference).
